sn13.3:1.2: The Ganges (Pali _gaṅgā_) is the greatest river of India. Arising far to the west in Uttarakhand, it flows 2,525 km, emptying into the Bay of Bengal in Bangladesh. The other rivers mentioned here are all its tributaries. | Yamunā is a major southern tributary of the Ganges, joining it at Payāga. It is an alternate name for the twin sister of Yama, god of the dead, Yamī for whom a shrine in maintained at Yamunotri, near the Yamunā’s source, Champasar Glacier. | Aciravatī is today the West Rapti, on whose banks Sāvatthī was located. Winding down from Nepal, it joins the Sarabhū to the north west of the confluence with the Ganges, in or near the land of the Kālāmas. | Sarabhū (Sanskrit _sarayū_) is the modern Gaghara, one of the largest northern tributaries of the Ganges, joining it west of Pāṭaliputta, modern Patna. | Mahī is the modern Kosi, which flows from Tibet through Nepal to join the Ganges in Aṅga, east of Pāṭaliputta around modern Kursela. | Also at [sn56.53]().
